name: Rust Cylinder
specific_features: Starship crash site (colony ship, warship, freighter)
description: Rust Cylinder is a small desert world dominated by iron oxide deposits that give every surface a deep, corroded red. The planet's most distinctive geological feature is a series of cylindrical mesas, towering columns of iron-rich stone carved by wind erosion into smooth, vertical-walled cylinders that rise hundreds of meters above the surrounding dust seas. Dead riverbeds wind between the cylinders, their courses marked by darker sediment that traces a world once wet enough for flowing water.

The thin atmosphere offers little protection from the searing daytime heat or the plunging nighttime cold, and the wind that sculpts the cylinder mesas carries iron-laden dust that coats everything in rust within days. The landscape has a mechanical, industrial quality, the smooth cylinders resembling the pistons and cylinders of some disassembled engine laid across the desert floor. Sound carries strangely between the cylinders, amplified and distorted by the smooth stone walls into echoes that persist for minutes.

An abandoned mining complex clings to the base of the largest cylinder, its prefabricated structures half-buried in drifting rust-colored sand. The miners extracted high-purity iron from the cylinder walls before a freighter crash destroyed their orbital transport capability, stranding the operation. The crashed freighter's remains are scattered across a dead riverbed to the east, its hull slowly being consumed by the same oxidation that colors the entire planet.

The iron deposits in the cylinder mesas are of exceptional purity and remain commercially valuable, though re-establishing transport infrastructure requires significant investment. The abandoned mining complex contains functional equipment and detailed geological surveys that would accelerate any new operation. Salvage rights to the crashed freighter are unclaimed, and its cargo manifest, if recoverable, may contain information about what else the mining operation was extracting besides the officially reported iron, as the complex's power consumption records suggest processing equipment far more sophisticated than iron refinement requires.
